claims.text: The initial Mg-containing lightweight HEA is a metastable single-phase solid solution.
Under service thermal conditions, the metastable solid solution transforms through nucleation and growth of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Phase separation into Mg-rich intermetallic compounds drives the alloy's microstructural evolution.
The resulting microstructural evolution dictates whether oxidation and corrosion resistance are retained or lost.
Aging at 600–800°C represents a service-relevant high-temperature treatment for the alloy.
Mg-rich intermetallic compounds preferentially emerge at grain boundaries or in specific intragranular regions.
High configurational entropy initially stabilizes the single-phase solid solution.
Thermal activation causes Mg atoms to diffuse and segregate.
Mg diffusion and segregation activate the nucleation and growth of intermetallic compounds.
Discrete, discontinuous intermetallic precipitates can act as local barriers to oxidation or corrosion.
A continuous intermetallic network can provide fast diffusion paths for deleterious species.
Thermally aged samples will contain detectable Mg-rich intermetallic phases that are absent from untreated samples.
A discontinuous precipitate distribution will retain or slightly improve oxidation and corrosion resistance relative to the initial state.
Formation of a continuous intermetallic network will significantly reduce oxidation and corrosion resistance relative to the initial state.
The untreated metastable alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
The untreated metastable alloy has inherently high corrosion and oxidation resistance.
Phase-separation kinetics are activated in the stated 600–800°C and corrosive service regimes.
The kinetics of Mg diffusion and intermetallic coalescence remain unquantified.
The effect of precipitate morphology on oxidation and corrosion performance remains unquantified and may vary with composition or processing.

Failure to form Mg-rich intermetallics, or failure of their presence and morphology to correlate with a measurable performance change relative to the untreated control, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
